title: The Flywheel and the Doom Loop
coreMove: Protect aligned momentum from the impulse to reset whenever progress is not yet dramatic.
sourcePressure: The source contrasts the flywheel with the doom loop: many consistent pushes in one direction create breakthrough, while reactive resets and transformation theater interrupt compounding.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version says be patient and never change anything.

exampleSpecs.audience: a blood bank director pressured to run a flashy awareness campaign
exampleSpecs.stakes: hospitals need reliable units more than one visible campaign spike
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director adds one repeat mobile site each month and refuses the billboard campaign after seeing donor return rates turn the supply wheel
exampleSpecs.firstImage: cooler seals lined in rows inside a mobile donation van

exampleSpecs.audience: a roaster tempted to rebrand after slow wholesale adoption
exampleSpecs.stakes: constant repositioning would reset trust before cafes see delivery reliability compound
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the roaster maps twelve weeks of on-time sample drops and sees the fourth cafe sign because of the prior three, then shelves the rebrand packet
exampleSpecs.firstImage: sample bags lined by roast date beside a delivery manifest

exampleSpecs.audience: a language-school director urged to scrap the curriculum after modest enrollment
exampleSpecs.stakes: switching methods every term prevents learners from compounding confidence
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director tracks phone-practice completions for six cohorts and keeps the method when retention rises before new enrollment does
exampleSpecs.firstImage: headset cords looped beside a wall of small progress stamps

exampleSpecs.audience: a transportation planner pressured to announce a new mobility initiative
exampleSpecs.stakes: residents need dependable cleared lanes more than a new slogan
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the planner points to traffic-counter gains after six months of weekly sweeping and declines the mayor's request to relaunch under a new name
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a paint stencil drying beside a curbside traffic counter

exampleSpecs.audience: a legal aid director deciding whether to pivot programs after slow early outcomes
exampleSpecs.stakes: tenants benefit when court clerks, shelters, and attorneys trust one repeat path
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director draws arrows from clerk referrals to shelter intake to hearing representation and shows that each push makes the next referral easier
exampleSpecs.firstImage: pink hearing notices sorted beside a courthouse intake stamp

exampleSpecs.audience: a studio lead facing pressure to rewrite the game after a quiet playtest
exampleSpecs.stakes: a reset would destroy months of tuning that is only now improving player return
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the lead compares crash reports, tutorial completions, and second-session returns, then keeps the engine and adds the next small tuning pass
exampleSpecs.firstImage: sticky build numbers glowing on a dark QA monitor

skillTargets: distinguish flywheel compounding from generic persistence
evaluate whether a change protects or interrupts momentum
trace how one aligned push makes the next easier

tryThisNowSpec: Write the last three aligned pushes in one effort and the next push that would make the fourth easier. Cross out any reset that only makes progress look new.

sourceAnchors.name: flywheel
sourceAnchors.detail: the source describes repeated aligned pushes that accumulate until momentum becomes visible to outsiders
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The flywheel looks ordinary while it is gaining weight, then obvious after the turns compound.

sourceAnchors.name: doom loop
sourceAnchors.detail: the source contrasts the flywheel with reactive resets, dramatic relaunches, and direction changes that interrupt momentum
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The doom loop is what happens when the organization keeps trading buildup for a fresh story.
